## (1) The failing line Q33, re-run

**Required change.** Three things:

* `Stamp` carries the restore generation beside the version.
* `isCurrent` and `assertStamp` compare the key, the generation and the version.
* A pin: a stamp taken before a cross-commit restore is stale after the same number of later commits, and a stamp
  taken after the restore is current.

It also requires that nothing persisted changes, and that restore-free callers behave as before.

**The code (read whole: `packages/kernel/src/arena/resolve.ts`).**

* `Stamp` gains `readonly generation?: number`.
* `stamp(p)` reads `restoreGeneration(p)` and writes the field only when it is not 0.
* `generationOf(s)` is `s.generation ?? 0`.
* `isCurrent` is `sameKey(stamp.key, p.key) && generationOf(stamp) === restoreGeneration(p) && stamp.version === p.version`.
* `assertStamp` checks in this order: the foreign key (message unchanged), then, under `debugAssertions()`, the
  generation (a new message), then the version (message unchanged).
* `resolve` spreads the stamp into each of the three views.
* The import `../tx/savepoint.js` is type-only on the savepoint side (`import type` only), so there is no runtime import
  cycle.

**The author's pins, green (CONFIRMED).** NEAR `test/arena` gives 12 files and 104 of 104 tests (see (2)). The
describe block `Q33: the stamp carries the restore generation (C-0309)` holds:

* the shape pin;
* n = 1 and n = 3 with the version coinciding;
* the same-version restore;
* the foreign key asserted first;
* the property over random commit / take / nested-restore / read sequences.

**This seat's probes (CONFIRMED, in the mirror, `test/tx/zz-close-s2.test.ts`, 8 tests).** All are green on the tree.

* **P1.** A real `tx` commit chain (`insertChain` batches) for n = 1 … 5. Every stamp read before the image and inside
  the rolled-back span is checked after the restore and after each of m = 0 … n + 2 further commits. It is stale at
  every step: `isCurrent` is false and `assertStamp` throws, including at the coinciding version. P1 reads three views:
  an edge role with geometry (`way:base`), a FaceRef (an owner with no faces) and an edge-role ref with no rows. Each fresh read carries `generation` 1, is current, and is stale
  after the next commit.
* **P2.** Two cross-commit restores. Generation-1 stamps at a version that coincides after the second restore are stale,
  and fresh stamps carry generation 2.
* **P3.** A real `tx` whose callback throws restores at its own version. The generation stays 0, the stamps stay
  current, and no field is written. In the non-debug build, `assertStamp` never throws, while `isCurrent` still answers
  false.

**Control.** On the old version-only code, planted as mutant K18 (no field, version-only `isCurrent` and
`assertStamp`), P1 – P3 go red: 7 of 8 tests. The author's pins go red too: 4 tests.

**Nothing persisted (CONFIRMED by grep).** `grep -rn "Resolved\|stampOf\|\bStamp\b\|isCurrent\|assertStamp"` over
`packages/kernel/src/{io,hash,digest}` and `packages/model/src/digest` finds only `digest/levelDigest.ts:616`'s
`isCurrent`, a local function over its own `State` (C-0308). No stamp is hashed, encoded or digested.

**Restore-free callers unchanged (CONFIRMED).**

* The only `src/` caller of `assertStamp` is `invariants/debug.ts` `debugAssertSlot`, and that function has no caller
  under `src/`. `isCurrent` has no `src/` caller outside the arena.
* `vitest related` reached `facade/stamps.test.ts`, `facade/reflection.test.ts`, `invariants/debug.test.ts`,
  `tx/savepoint.test.ts`, the arena folder and 461 files in all. Every red is attributed below.
* In the buffer agreement test, instrumentation shows no `restoreSavepoint` call at all, so the generation stays 0
  there. That makes the new code byte-for-byte equivalent to the old there.

## Targeted mutants (18; one at a time in the mirror)

Each mutant was run against two test sets:

* **NEAR + stamps:** `test/arena`, `test/facade/stamps.test.ts`, `test/facade/reflection.test.ts`,
  `test/invariants/debug.test.ts` and `test/tx/savepoint.test.ts`. Baseline: 140 of 140 green.
* **probe:** this seat's P1 – P3. Baseline: 8 of 8 green.

| mutant | promise aimed at | NEAR + stamps | probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 `isCurrent` version-only (the Q33 fault) | isCurrent keys on generation | RED 4 | RED 7 |
| K2 `isCurrent` drops the version | isCurrent keys on version | RED 4 | RED 5 |
| K3 `isCurrent` drops the key | foreign key | RED 2 | green |
| K4 `assertStamp` drops the generation check | assertStamp keys on generation | RED 3 | RED 6 |
| K5 `assertStamp` drops the version check | version message unchanged | RED 5 | RED 5 |
| K6 `assertStamp` accepts an older generation (`<=`) | equality of generation | RED 3 | RED 6 |
| K7 the stamp never writes the generation | the stamp carries it | RED 3 | RED 6 |
| K8 the stamp always writes the generation | restore-free shape unchanged | RED 2 | RED 1 |
| K9 the stamp writes generation + 1 | the stamp reads `restoreGeneration(p)` | RED 3 | RED 6 |
| K10 an absent generation reads 1 | absent reads 0 | RED 8 | RED 7 |
| K11 `generationOf` ignores the stamp | — | RED 4 | RED 6 |
| K12 the generation check before the key check | the foreign key asserts first | RED 2 | green |
| K13 the generation check ungated by the debug flag | a no-op when the build does not assert | RED 2 | RED 1 |
| K14 `isCurrent` generation OR version | conjunction | RED 5 | RED 7 |
| K15 the faces view drops the generation | every view carries it | **green** | RED 6 |
| K16 the edges view drops the generation | every view carries it | **green** | RED 6 |
| K17 the generation cached per arena at first read | read at each stamp | RED 3 | RED 6 |
| K18 the old code (K1 + K4 + K7) | the whole fix | RED 4 | RED 7 |

16 of 18 mutants are red on the item's tests.

K15 and K16 survive them. Each rewrites one view's object literal so that it leaves out the `...s` spread, which every
view now shares. The code keeps the promise for all three views: P1 is green on the tree and red under both mutants
(CONFIRMED). The failure each mutant would introduce is loud, not silent: a fresh stamp reads stale and asserts.

So this is a missing hardening test, not a wrong result. It is filed as N-s2-1 (M4), as round S1's K11 was. It was not
judged equivalent.

## Refusal count (ZERO REFUSALS, J264), re-measured

**Measurement (CONFIRMED).** In the mirror, every structural `check` refusal (arena `debug.ts`) and every debug
assertion (`resolve.ts`) was logged. The arena folder was run at `PLAT_FUZZ_SEED=12345` twice: on the version-only code
("before") and on the tree's code ("after").

**Structural refusals: 128 before and 128 after, line for line identical.** All of them come from the deliberate
malformed-input and full-table tests, which is unlawful input. Examples:

* `an owner table is full` ×8;
* `a role-head table is full` ×8;
* `a table capacity is a power of two` ×7.

The only difference between the two runs is the count of `a stale slot` debug assertions. These come from tests that
pass stale stamps on purpose (a programming error, never a KernelResult). On the old code the Q33 property stops at its
first counterexample, which explains the different count.

**Lawful-input refusals of the item's families: 0 before, 0 after.** The families are the arena's fixtures, the 10⁶-op
head-table and handle properties, the size arena and the stamp property. All of them are green with no refusal outcome,
and the round adds no refusal path. The count did not rise.

## (3) New findings: notes only (`checks/M0-a-02-notes.md`)

* **N-s2-1 (KI, M4).** K15 and K16 survive. Pin a FaceRef and an edge-role read after the restore.
* **N-s2-2 (cross-item, M0-a-16; the Q33 class; the session's call).** The façade's `stamp` / `stampWith` /
  `inlineStamp` / `assertStamped` key on the version alone. Probe P4 CONFIRMED that a façade Resolved read in a
  rolled-back commit passes `kernel.assertCurrent` silently after restore + 1 commit: its `stampOf` is `{key,
  version: 2}` with no generation. On the same value the arena's `assertStamp` throws. C-0309 (5)(a) reports this, but
  it is not in M0-FIX-QUEUE.
* **N-s2-3 (KI, M0-a-15, M4).** `compactSlots` copies key and version, so a stamp of the original reads current on the
  copy. Probe P5: half-edge 20 on `p`, 6 on `q`. This predates the round.
* **N-s2-4 (session).** The buffer agreement test's reduced-size cap is 1 and it does not replay from `PLAT_FUZZ_SEED`
  (see (2)).

None of these is a blocker under the brief's rule:

* every gate exits 0 apart from attributed foreign reds;
